title: An Ideal Student Paragraph
excerpt: On this page you will find an ideal student paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes,
plainContent: On this page you will find an ideal student paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. An Ideal Student Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. An ideal student is a student who treats education as a responsibility, not only as a race for marks. He attends classes regularly, listens to his teachers carefully, and asks questions when he does not understand a lesson. He studies every day, reviews his lessons before they are forgotten, and tries to understand ideas instead of memorising them without meaning. An ideal student is also good in character. He respects his parents, teachers, and classmates, and follows the rules of his school. He is truthful, punctual, and helpful, and he admits his mistakes honestly. He keeps his body healthy through exercise, sleep, and play, because a healthy body helps concentration. He does not become proud after success or hopeless after failure. He helps weaker classmates, keeps his notes organised, and uses his time well. In this way, he prepares himself not only for examinations but also for a useful life. An Ideal Student Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. An ideal student is a student who treats education as a responsibility rather than a race for marks. Such a learner attends classes regularly, listens carefully, asks questions, and reviews lessons before they are forgotten. Instead of memorising every sentence, the student tries to understand ideas and explain them independently. He keeps a daily routine for study, revision, and rest, and he completes his homework and classwork on time. He prepares his lessons before class so that he can follow the teacher easily and take part in discussion. Good study is balanced with good character. An ideal student respects parents, teachers, classmates, and school rules. The student is truthful, punctual, helpful, and willing to admit mistakes. He never copies in examinations and never looks down on weaker students. He avoids gossip and useless activities in his free time. Instead, he helps his classmates, shares his notes, and learns from group study. Exercise, sleep, and recreation are also important because a healthy body supports concentration and a fresh mind learns faster. An excellent learner does not become proud after success or discouraged after failure. He finds out why he failed, corrects his weakness, and tries again with more care. He uses technology responsibly, for learning and research, not for wasting time. He also takes part in social service and school activities when he gets time. These habits prepare a person not only for examinations but also for useful citizenship. True excellence combines knowledge, discipline, kindness, and the courage to keep improving. An Ideal Student Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. An ideal student is one who treats education as a responsibility rather than a race for marks. He understands that student life is the best time to build knowledge, character, and good habits for the future. So he attends classes regularly, listens to his teachers with attention, and asks questions whenever he does not understand a lesson. He studies every day according to a routine, reviews his lessons before they are forgotten, and completes his homework on time. Instead of memorising every sentence without meaning, he tries to understand ideas deeply and explain them in his own words. He keeps his notes organised and reads reference books. But good marks alone do not make an ideal student. Character matters just as much as study. An ideal student respects his parents, teachers, and classmates, and he follows the rules of his school and society. He is truthful, punctual, honest, and helpful. He admits his mistakes, keeps his promises, and never cheats in examinations. He is kind to weaker classmates and learns from others without pride. He keeps his body healthy through regular exercise, enough sleep, and outdoor games, because a healthy body supports a fresh and attentive mind. An ideal student also knows how to face both success and failure. Success does not make him proud, and failure does not make him hopeless. When he fails, he finds the reason, corrects his weakness, and works harder the next time. He uses mobile phones and the internet responsibly, mainly for learning, and avoids wasting hours on useless entertainment. He joins social service and school activities, which teach leadership and responsibility. In this way, an ideal student prepares himself not only for examinations but also for a useful and honourable life. True excellence is the combination of knowledge, discipline, kindness, and the courage to keep improving every day. title: Tree Plantation paragraph
excerpt: Tree plantation means deliberately growing trees in suitable places and caring for them. It is important in Bangladesh because trees provide oxygen, shade,
plainContent: Tree Plantation Tree plantation means deliberately growing trees in suitable places and caring for them. It is important in Bangladesh because trees provide oxygen, shade, fruit, wood, soil protection, and habitats for birds and other animals. Their roots help reduce erosion, while leaves cool the surroundings and improve air quality. We can plant trees beside roads, around schools, near ponds, on unused land, and in home gardens. Fruit trees can provide food and income, while native shade trees benefit people and wildlife. A planting programme should select healthy saplings, prepare the soil, water them regularly, and protect them from grazing animals. Planting without later care often leads to failure. People should stop unnecessary cutting and replace trees that must be removed. Schools and local groups can observe a tree-planting day, but caring for the saplings throughout the year is more important than a ceremony. By increasing green spaces and protecting old trees, we help the climate, soil, economy, and health of our communities. Every household and institution can contribute.

plainContent: A publication made by a school community A school magazine is a collection of writing and artwork prepared by students and teachers. It may appear once a year and include poems, essays, short stories, reports, drawings, puzzles, interviews, and records of important school events. A teacher usually guides the editorial committee, while students collect submissions, edit drafts, arrange illustrations, and check proofs. The process teaches planning, cooperation, careful reading, and respect for other people’s ideas. A student who is quiet in class may discover confidence after seeing a poem or report printed in the magazine. The publication also preserves the character of the school during a particular year. Readers can learn about achievements, clubs, celebrations, and community projects. A magazine should welcome different abilities rather than publish only perfect writing. With encouragement and honest editing, it becomes both a record of school life and a training ground for future communicators.

plainContent: A quiet morning in the cold season A winter morning arrives slowly under a veil of mist. Before sunrise, trees and rooftops look blurred, and the familiar road seems shorter because the fog hides its far end. The air feels sharp, so people wrap themselves in shawls, sweaters, or blankets. The scene changes when the sun rises. Golden light gradually burns away the mist, dew shines on grass, and birds begin to call from the branches. Farmers lead their cattle to the fields, while children hurry to school after warming themselves beside a small fire. Tea stalls become popular because a hot cup gives workers comfort before the day begins. Winter mornings are especially pleasant to those who can enjoy them at leisure. Date juice, cakes, fresh vegetables, and warm sunshine are seasonal pleasures. Yet poor people often suffer because they lack warm clothing and shelter. We should share blankets and food with neighbours who need help. A winter morning combines beauty, freshness, and hardship. Its peaceful atmosphere is memorable, but its human lesson is equally important: comfort should not make us forget the vulnerable.

plainContent: Load Shedding Load shedding is the planned interruption of electricity when demand is greater than the available supply or when the power network needs protection. It may also occur because of fuel shortages, damaged equipment, storms, or faults in transmission lines. An unexpected power cut disturbs homes, schools, hospitals, shops, factories, and farms. Students cannot study comfortably, food may spoil in a refrigerator, water pumps may stop, and businesses can lose working hours. Hospitals need generators and careful planning because many patients depend on electrical equipment. Repeated cuts can also damage appliances when the current returns suddenly. The problem can be reduced by producing sufficient electricity, repairing the grid, preventing illegal connections, and using renewable sources such as solar power. Consumers should switch off unnecessary lights and fans, use energy-efficient appliances, and avoid wasting electricity during peak periods. Authorities should publish reliable schedules and give priority to essential services. Responsible use by citizens, combined with investment in generation and distribution, can make the supply more dependable.

title: How to Write an Application: Format, Examples & Tips
excerpt: Application writing is an important part of English writing in Bangladesh. Students may need to write an application to the headmaster, principal, department
plainContent: Application writing is an important part of English writing in Bangladesh. Students may need to write an application to the headmaster, principal, department head, or another authority for different reasons. For example, you may need to write an application for leave, a testimonial, a transfer certificate, permission for a study tour, or another school or college matter. University students and job seekers also write formal applications for academic and professional purposes. The good news is that most formal applications follow a simple structure. Once you understand the format, you can write an application for almost any situation. This guide explains the basic application writing format and provides examples for school, college, university, and job applications. What Is an Application? An application is a formal written request made to a person or authority. For example: A student writes to the headmaster for leave. A student writes to the principal for a testimonial. A university student writes to the examination office for a transcript. A student writes to an authority for permission to join a study tour. A job seeker writes to an employer to apply for a position. The purpose of an application should be clear from the beginning. Avoid unnecessary information and explain exactly what you are requesting. Basic Application Writing Format A formal application usually contains these parts: Date Name and designation of the recipient Institution or organisation Address Subject Salutation Main body Closing Name and identifying information of the applicant A simple structure looks like this: Date The [Designation] [Institution Name] [Address] Subject: Application for [purpose]. Sir/Madam, First paragraph: Introduce yourself and explain why you are writing. Second paragraph: Give the necessary details about your situation. Final paragraph: Clearly state what you are requesting. Yours faithfully/obediently, [Your Name] [Class/Department] [Roll/ID] The exact format can vary between institutions, so students should follow any specific instructions given by their school, college, university, or employer. 1. Application for Leave A leave application is written when you need permission to remain absent from school, college, or another institution. Example: Leave Application for Illness 15 January 2026 The Headmaster Ideal High School Motijheel, Dhaka Subject: Application for leave of absence. Sir, With due respect, I would like to inform you that I am a student of Class IX, Section B, of your school. I have been suffering from a high fever for the last three days, and the doctor has advised me to take rest. For this reason, I will not be able to attend school from 15 January to 18 January 2026. I therefore request you to kindly grant me leave for these four days. I shall be grateful for your kind consideration. Yours obediently, Md. Rakib Hasan Class IX, Section B Roll No. 17 What to include in a leave application Make sure you mention: The reason for your absence The dates of your leave Your class or department Your roll or student ID Any supporting document if the institution requires one Do not write a long explanation. Give only the information the authority needs. 2. Application for a Testimonial A testimonial is an official document that may provide information about a student's academic record, conduct, or period of study at an institution. Students may need a testimonial after completing SSC or HSC or when applying for further education or other purposes. Example: Testimonial Application 10 February 2026 The Principal Dhaka College New Market, Dhaka Subject: Application for a testimonial. Sir, With due respect, I would like to inform you that I passed the HSC examination in 2025 from your college under the Dhaka Education Board. I am now preparing to apply for higher studies and require a testimonial from the college. I therefore request you to kindly issue me a testimonial at your earliest convenience. I shall be grateful for your kind consideration. Yours obediently, Sumaiya Akter HSC 2025, Science Group Roll No. 124356 Tip for students If the institution has a specific testimonial form, use that form instead of writing a separate application. Some Bangladeshi institutions provide their own testimonial forms with fields for student information and academic details. 3. Application for an Academic Transcript University students may need an academic transcript when applying for higher studies, scholarships, employment, or other official purposes. The procedure is different from one university to another. Some universities require a specific form, fee payment, clearance, or supporting documents. Example 22 March 2026 The Controller of Examinations University of Dhaka Dhaka-1000 Subject: Application for issuance of academic transcript. Sir, With due respect, I would like to inform you that I completed my Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science and Engineering from your university in 2025. I now require an official academic transcript for my application for higher studies abroad. I have completed the required payment and attached the necessary documents with this application. I therefore request you to kindly issue two copies of my official academic transcript. Yours faithfully, Mohammad Tanvir Ahmed Registration No. 2021-715-001 Session: 2020–2021 Department of CSE Important Before submitting a university application, check your university's current instructions. Do not assume that every university uses the same process. 4. Application for a Transfer Certificate A transfer certificate application is generally written when a student needs official permission or documentation to leave one institution and continue studies elsewhere. Example 20 April 2026 The Principal ABC College Dhaka Subject: Application for a transfer certificate. Sir, With due respect, I would like to inform you that I am a student of Class XII of your college. My family is moving to another city, and I need to continue my studies there. I therefore request you to kindly issue me a transfer certificate so that I can complete the necessary admission formalities at another institution. I shall be grateful for your kind consideration. Yours obediently, Rahim Ahmed Class XII Roll No. 25 Science Group 5. Application for Permission to Join a Study Tour Students may need permission from their school or college authority before joining an educational tour or study tour. Example 5 May 2026 The Headmaster ABC High School Dhaka Subject: Application for permission to join a study tour. Sir, With due respect, we, the students of Class X, would like to arrange an educational study tour to the National Museum in Dhaka. Such a visit would give us an opportunity to learn more about the history and culture of Bangladesh outside the classroom. We therefore request you to kindly grant us permission to arrange the study tour under the guidance of our teachers. We shall be grateful for your kind consideration. Yours obediently, The students of Class X ABC High School Dhaka Tip For a group application, write on behalf of the students and clearly mention the proposed destination, purpose, and supervision arrangements when relevant. 6. Job Application Letter A job application is different from a school application. Instead of asking a school authority for permission or a document, you are introducing yourself to an employer and explaining why you are suitable for a particular position. A modern job application should be concise and specific. Example 5 April 2026 The Head of Human Resources ABC Bank Limited Gulshan, Dhaka Subject: Application for the position of Management Trainee Officer. Dear Sir/Madam, I am writing to apply for the position of Management Trainee Officer advertised on your company's website. I recently completed my BBA in Finance from North South University with a CGPA of 3.78. During my undergraduate studies, I completed a three-month internship with a commercial bank, where I gained practical experience in credit analysis and customer service. I believe my academic background, internship experience, and communication skills would allow me to contribute effectively to your organisation. My CV and relevant academic documents are attached for your consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my qualifications in an interview. Yours faithfully, Nusrat Jahan nusrat.jahan@example.com +880 1XXX-XXXXXX Job application tip Do not copy the same application for every job. Mention the actual position, organisation, and skills that are relevant to the job. Your application should support your CV rather than repeat everything in it. 7. Application for a Character Certificate A character certificate or similar official document may be requested for admission, employment, or other purposes. The exact name and procedure can vary by institution. Example 12 June 2026 The Headmaster ABC High School Dhaka Subject: Application for a character certificate. Sir, With due respect, I would like to inform you that I was a student of your school and passed the SSC examination in 2026. I now require a character certificate for my further studies. I therefore request you to kindly issue me a character certificate mentioning my conduct and period of study at the institution. I shall be grateful for your kind consideration. Yours obediently, Sadia Islam SSC 2026 Roll No. 123456 How to Write an Application Step by Step If you have never written a formal application before, follow these steps. Step 1: Identify the person you are writing to Find out who should receive the application. For example: The Headmaster The Principal The Head of the Department The Controller of Examinations The Human Resources Manager Use the correct designation. Step 2: Write a clear subject The subject should tell the reader what you want. Good examples: Application for leave of absence Application for a testimonial Application for issuance of an academic transcript Application for a transfer certificate Application for permission to join a study tour Do not write a long subject. Step 3: Introduce yourself Tell the reader who you are. For example: I am a student of Class X, Section A, of your school. A university student could write: I am a student of the Department of Computer Science and Engineering. Step 4: Explain the reason Give the important facts related to your request. For a leave application, mention the reason and dates. For a testimonial, explain why you need it. For a transcript, explain what you need and, if relevant, what the transcript is for. Step 5: Make your request clearly Do not make the reader guess what you want. For example: I therefore request you to kindly grant me leave for three days. Step 6: End politely Use an appropriate formal closing. For example: I shall be grateful for your kind consideration. Then add your name and relevant identification details. Common Mistakes in Application Writing Students often make simple mistakes that can make an application look careless. 1. Forgetting the subject The subject helps the reader understand the purpose of the application quickly. 2. Writing too much A formal application should contain the information necessary to understand and process the request. Avoid unrelated stories. 3. Using informal language Avoid expressions such as: Hi Sir What's up I wanna request Please help me out Thanks a lot Use polite and formal language instead. 4. Using unnecessary difficult words You do not need complicated English to write a good application. For example: I would like to request you to kindly grant me leave. is clear and sufficient. A simple sentence is usually better than a long sentence filled with difficult words. 5. Forgetting personal details For school and college applications, include the details needed to identify you, such as: Name Class Section Roll number Registration number Department Student ID Only include information that is relevant to the application. 6. Using the wrong closing Choose the closing according to the situation and the style required by your institution. For traditional school applications, “Yours obediently” is commonly used. For professional applications, “Yours faithfully” or “Yours sincerely” may be more appropriate depending on how you address the recipient. Yours Obediently, Yours Faithfully, or Yours Sincerely? These expressions are often confusing for students. Yours obediently This is commonly found in traditional school and college applications addressed to teachers or institutional authorities. Yours faithfully This is commonly used in formal correspondence when you do not address the recipient by name, especially in British-style business writing. Example: Dear Sir/Madam, Yours faithfully, Yours sincerely This is commonly used when you address the recipient by name. Example: Dear Mr Karim, Yours sincerely, However, institutions may have their own preferred format. If your school or university gives you a prescribed format, follow it. Application Writing Format for SSC and HSC Students For SSC and HSC students, application writing is also an important part of English writing practice. Common topics include: Application for leave Application for a testimonial Application for a transfer certificate Application for a seat in the school hostel Application for permission to arrange a study tour Application for setting up a canteen Application for improving library facilities Application for arranging a cultural programme For examination practice, first understand the format. Then practise writing different applications instead of memorising one answer word for word. A memorised application may not fit a new question exactly. Application Writing vs. Formal Letter Writing These two types of writing are related, but they have different purposes. An application is usually a formal request made to an authority. A formal letter can have a wider purpose, such as making a complaint, requesting information, giving notice, or communicating with an organisation. For example: Application: Application to the principal for leave. Formal letter: Letter to the editor about traffic congestion in Dhaka. Knowing the purpose helps you choose the right format. Quick Application Writing Template You can use this template when you need to write a new application. [Date] The [Designation] [Institution Name] [Address] Subject: Application for [purpose]. Sir/Madam, With due respect, I would like to inform you that I am [your position/class/department]. [Explain the reason for your application and provide the important details.] I therefore request you to kindly [clearly state what you want]. I shall be grateful for your kind consideration. Yours faithfully/obediently, [Your Name] [Class/Department] [Roll/Student ID] Use this as a framework, not as a paragraph to memorise. Change the details and sentences according to the situation. Frequently Asked Questions What is the format of an application in Bangladesh? A formal application generally includes the date, recipient's designation and institution, subject, salutation, body, closing, and the applicant's identifying details. The exact format may vary depending on the institution. How do I start an application? Start by identifying the recipient and writing a clear subject. In the first paragraph, introduce yourself and explain the reason for writing. How long should a formal application be? For most school and college applications, one or two short paragraphs are enough. Include the necessary information without adding unrelated details. Should I write an application by hand? Follow the instructions of the institution or organisation. Some schools may prefer handwritten applications, while universities and employers may require typed or online submissions. What paper size should I use? If the institution has not specified a paper size, A4 is a practical choice for a typed formal document. However, always follow the instructions provided by the receiving institution. Can I use the same application format for every topic? You can use the same basic structure, but the content should change according to your purpose. A leave application, testimonial application, university transcript request, and job application should not contain the same body text. Should I memorise application examples for exams? It is better to understand the format and practise different topics. Memorising complete applications can make it difficult to answer questions that use a different situation. Final Tips for Writing a Good Application Before submitting your application, check these points: Is the recipient correct? Is the subject clear? Did you explain the reason? Did you make your request clear? Did you include your class, roll, ID, or department where necessary? Did you use polite and formal language? Did you check spelling and grammar? Did you follow any instructions given by the institution? Did you remove unnecessary information? A good application does not need complicated English. It needs a clear purpose, correct information, polite language, and a suitable format. Once you understand the basic structure, you can write applications for school, college, university, and professional situations with much more confidence.

title: Air Pollution Paragraph
excerpt: Air pollution occurs when smoke, dust, poisonous gases, or tiny particles enter the atmosphere in harmful amounts. Vehicle exhaust, brick kilns, factories,
plainContent: When the air becomes unsafe Air pollution occurs when smoke, dust, poisonous gases, or tiny particles enter the atmosphere in harmful amounts. Vehicle exhaust, brick kilns, factories, burning rubbish, construction work, and forest fires are common sources. In crowded cities, pollution can become especially serious when wind is weak. Breathing polluted air may irritate the eyes and throat and can worsen asthma, heart disease, and other respiratory problems. Children, older people, and outdoor workers are often most vulnerable. Pollution also damages crops, buildings, animals, and the climate. The solution requires both public policy and personal responsibility. Authorities can enforce emission standards, improve public transport, control construction dust, and promote clean energy. Citizens can avoid burning waste, maintain vehicles, plant suitable trees, and walk or share transport when possible. Schools can teach children to notice local pollution and support clean-air campaigns. Protecting the atmosphere is a shared duty because everyone depends on healthy air.

plainContent: On this page you will find a My Hobby paragraph in 150, 250 and 300 words for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC. The short version is best for junior classes, the longer versions are best for SSC and HSC. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. My Hobby Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. My favourite hobby is gardening. I grow flowers, herbs, and a few vegetables in pots and in a small patch beside our home. I loosen the soil, sow seeds, water the plants, and remove weeds. Watching a seed become a living plant teaches me patience and care. Gardening refreshes me after study and gives me gentle exercise. Green plants make the surroundings cooler and more attractive, while herbs and vegetables can provide fresh food. I reuse kitchen containers as planters and avoid wasting water. Sometimes I share seedlings with my neighbours. This hobby has made me more interested in nature and more aware that healthy surroundings depend on daily responsibility. I also keep a small diary where I write the names of new plants and note when I sowed their seeds. This diary helps me remember what worked and what did not. My Hobby Paragraph in 250 Words Best for Class 8–10 and SSC. My favourite hobby is gardening. I grow flowers, herbs, and a few vegetables in pots and in a small patch beside our home. I loosen the soil, sow seeds, water the plants, and remove weeds. Watching a seed become a living plant teaches me patience and care, because a plant does not grow in a single day. I have learned the names of many plants and flowers, and I enjoy seeing bees and butterflies visit my garden. Gardening refreshes me after study and gives me gentle exercise. It takes my mind away from books and mobile screens for a while, and the fresh air makes me feel calm. Green plants make the surroundings cooler and more attractive, while herbs and vegetables can provide fresh food for my family. I reuse kitchen containers as planters, collect rainwater when I can, and avoid wasting water. Sometimes I share seedlings with my neighbours, and we exchange advice about plants. This hobby has made me more interested in nature and more aware that healthy surroundings depend on daily responsibility. A small garden can teach us that good results need regular work, not only big plans. On weekends, I sometimes visit a nursery to learn about new plants and to buy seeds for the next season. The nursery workers often give useful advice about soil, water, and sunlight, and I try to follow their suggestions at home. Gardening has also taught me the value of patience, because a garden rewards those who wait and work steadily. My Hobby Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. My favourite hobby is gardening. Green plants make the surroundings cooler and more attractive, while herbs and vegetables can provide fresh food for my family. A garden also helps the environment, because plants give oxygen and keep the air clean. I reuse kitchen containers as planters, collect rainwater when I can, and avoid wasting water. plainContent: The consequences of cutting forests Trees are being removed for fuel, timber, roads, farms, and construction. When this clearing continues without replanting, the result is deforestation. It destroys animal habitats, weakens soil, reduces rainfall absorption, and adds to global warming because fewer trees remain to take in carbon dioxide. Deforested land is more likely to suffer erosion, floods, drought, and extreme heat. People who depend on forests for food, medicine, or work also lose important resources. The damage can continue for many years after the last tree is cut. We should protect natural forests, enforce laws against illegal logging, and restore damaged land with suitable species. Schools and families can plant and care for trees, reduce wasteful paper use, and teach others why forests matter. Conservation is a shared duty because healthy forests support a healthy society.

plainContent: Physical Exercise Physical exercise is the movement of the body in a planned and healthy way. Walking, swimming, cycling, running, gardening, games, and sports can all keep us active. Exercise makes muscles stronger, improves blood circulation, supports a healthy weight, and helps the mind remain fresh. A young and fit person may choose a sport or a brisk run, while an elderly or weak person can begin with gentle walking and stretching. No single activity is suitable for everyone. Facebook Paragraph in 150 Words Best for Class 6–7. Facebook is a social networking service that connects people across the world. Users can create a profile, add friends, share photographs and videos, join groups, follow news pages, and send messages. It helps relatives and friends who live far apart stay in touch, and it helps students learn new things through educational pages and groups. Small businesses also use Facebook to show their products and reach customers. However, Facebook has some dangers. False news spreads quickly, and strangers can misuse personal information. Spending too much time scrolling can waste study time and disturb sleep. Users should keep their privacy settings strong, accept friend requests carefully, and never share passwords or personal details with strangers. They should check a news item before sharing it and use polite language in comments. Facebook is useful when it is used for learning and communication, but it becomes harmful when it replaces study, sleep, and real friendship. plainContent: A changing climate and our responsibility The climate is changing because large amounts of heat-trapping gases are entering the atmosphere. Vehicles, factories, power stations, and the destruction of forests all contribute to this increase. A warmer planet can bring irregular rain, longer heat waves, melting ice, stronger storms, and rising sea levels. These effects are serious for Bangladesh. Floods and cyclones can damage homes and crops, while salt water may enter fields and drinking-water sources. Poor families usually suffer most because they have fewer resources to rebuild. We cannot solve the problem through one action. Public authorities should protect forests, develop clean energy, improve warning systems, and plan climate-resilient towns. Citizens can conserve electricity, plant and protect trees, reduce waste, and use buses or bicycles when practical. Education is important because informed people make better choices. Climate change is not a distant issue. Careful decisions today can reduce future damage and protect the lives and livelihoods of coming generations.

plainContent: Price Hike A price hike is a sustained increase in the cost of everyday goods and services. When rice, vegetables, fuel, medicine, rent, or transport becomes more expensive, families must spend more for the same standard of living. The burden is especially heavy for workers whose salaries do not rise with the market. Prices may increase because of inflation, higher fuel and production costs, floods or other disasters, shortages, currency changes, transport problems, hoarding, and excessive profit-taking. A disruption in one part of the supply chain can affect the final price in a shop. The result can be anxiety, reduced nutrition, postponed treatment, and greater poverty. The government can respond by ensuring adequate supply, improving storage and transport, monitoring markets, taking action against illegal hoarding, and assisting families in genuine difficulty. Farmers and small traders also need fair access to finance and markets. Consumers should compare prices, avoid waste, and not create artificial shortages by panic buying. A coordinated effort can protect both producers and buyers while the economy stabilises.

plainContent: Small help, great value A lion was sleeping beneath a tree when a mouse ran across his paw. The lion caught the little creature and prepared to punish it. The mouse begged for freedom and promised that it might help him someday. The lion laughed at the unlikely idea but released it. Some time later, hunters trapped the lion in a strong net. His loud roars reached the mouse, which hurried to the place. Using its sharp teeth, it gnawed through the ropes one strand at a time. Soon the lion was free, and he understood that size does not determine usefulness. The lion thanked the mouse and changed his view of weaker creatures. Everyone has abilities that may become valuable in an unexpected situation. Kindness also creates bonds that return when help is needed. Moral: Never despise a small friend; kindness is rarely wasted.

plainContent: On this page you will find a letter about how to improve English, written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. You can learn the letter for your examination and also follow its advice to improve your English at the same time. Format Your address at the top of the letter, on the right or left side as your teacher advises. The date below your address, so the reader knows when you wrote the letter. A greeting or salutation, such as "Dear Tuhin," to the friend you are writing to. The body of the letter, in three or four short paragraphs, with your main ideas in order. A closing line, such as "With love," followed by your name at the end of the letter. Simple and correct English throughout, with short sentences that are easy to understand. Letter: How to Improve English (Example) Dear Tuhin, I hope you are well. Thank you for your letter. You asked me how I am improving my English, so I am writing to share the simple methods that are helping me most. English is important for our studies, for good jobs and for learning about the world, so I try to practise it a little every day instead of studying it only before an examination. First, I read something in English every day. I read a short story, a newspaper article or a lesson from my textbook, and I note down useful expressions, not only single words. Then I listen to clear English conversations and repeat the sentences aloud, so my pronunciation and speaking become better. I also speak in English with a friend for a few minutes every day, even if I make mistakes. Second, I write a little every day. I write a diary entry or a short paragraph, and then I check the spelling and grammar carefully. I keep a vocabulary notebook and try to use each new word in a sentence of my own, because a word is easy to remember when I use it myself. I use a dictionary when I do not know a word, but I do not memorise long lists without understanding them. When I make a mistake, I correct it and try again, because correction is a natural part of learning. I hope these ideas will help you too. Start with fifteen minutes a day, and increase the time slowly when you feel comfortable. With patience and regular practice, your reading, writing, listening and speaking will all become stronger. Please write back soon and tell me how your practice is going. plainContent: On this page you will find a letter about brilliant success, written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. It gives the format of a personal letter, a full example letter congratulating a friend on an excellent SSC result, its Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. You can learn the letter for your examination and use it to congratulate a friend in real life too. Format Your address at the top of the letter, on the right or left side as your teacher advises. The date below your address, so the reader knows when you wrote the letter. A greeting or salutation, such as "Dear Tanvir," to the friend you are writing to. The body of the letter, in three or four short paragraphs, with your congratulations, the reason for them, and your good wishes for the future. A closing line, such as "With best wishes," followed by your name at the end of the letter. Simple and correct English throughout, with short sentences that are easy to understand. Letter: Congratulations on Brilliant Success (Example) Dear Tanvir, I was delighted to hear that you achieved an excellent result in the SSC examination. Please accept my warm congratulations. Your success is the reward for your regular study, careful preparation and strong determination. You studied every day, followed your routine, and never gave up even when a lesson was difficult. I am very happy for you, and I know how proud your parents and teachers must feel today. Your result has brought pride and happiness to your whole family. Your parents worked hard for you, and your teachers guided you with care, so this success belongs to their love and support as well as to your own effort. Your friends are also glad to see you do so well. A good result like this does not come by luck alone; it comes from honest work, patience and discipline over a long time. Do not become careless after this achievement. Success is only the beginning of a longer journey, and the next stage will need the same hard work. Continue learning with the same discipline, choose your next course thoughtfully, and set a clear goal for your future. Take advice from your parents and teachers before you decide, because a good decision now will help you for many years. I am sure that your honesty and hard work will help you reach an even brighter goal. Keep your good habits, stay humble, and help your classmates who are still trying to improve. I pray that you will do even better in the HSC examination and in your life ahead. Please convey my respects to your parents. With best wishes, Rahim Bangla Meaning অসাধারণ সাফল্যের চিঠির বাংলা অর্থ প্রিয় তানভীর, এসএসসি পরীক্ষায় তুমি চমৎকার ফলাফল করেছ শুনে আমি খুব আনন্দিত হয়েছি। আমার আন্তরিক অভিনন্দন গ্রহণ করো। তোমার এই সাফল্য তোমার নিয়মিত পড়াশোনা, যত্নশীল প্রস্তুতি ও দৃঢ় সংকল্পের পুরস্কার। তুমি প্রতিদিন পড়েছ, নিজের রুটিন মেনে চলেছ এবং কোনো পাঠ কঠিন হলেও হাল ছাড়োনি। আমি তোমার জন্য খুব খুশি, আর জানি আজ তোমার বাবা-মা ও শিক্ষকেরা কতটা গর্বিত। তোমার ফলাফল তোমার পুরো পরিবারের জন্য গর্ব ও আনন্দ বয়ে এনেছে। তোমার বাবা-মা তোমার জন্য অনেক কষ্ট করেছেন এবং তোমার শিক্ষকেরা যত্নে তোমাকে পথ দেখিয়েছেন, তাই এই সাফল্য তোমার নিজের চেষ্টার পাশাপাশি তাঁদের ভালোবাসা ও সহযোগিতারও ফসল। তোমার বন্ধুরাও তোমার ভালো ফল দেখে খুশি। এমন ভালো ফল শুধু ভাগ্যে আসে না; তা আসে দীর্ঘদিনের সৎ পরিশ্রম, ধৈর্য ও শৃঙ্খলা থেকে। এই অর্জনের পর অসতর্ক হয়ো না। সাফল্য কেবল একটি দীর্ঘ যাত্রার শুরু, আর পরের ধাপেও একই পরিশ্রম দরকার হবে। একই শৃঙ্খলা নিয়ে পড়াশোনা চালিয়ে যাও, ভেবেচিন্তে তোমার পরের পাঠক্রমটি বেছে নাও এবং ভবিষ্যতের জন্য একটি স্পষ্ট লক্ষ্য ঠিক করো। সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়ার আগে বাবা-মা ও শিক্ষকদের পরামর্শ নাও, কারণ এখনকার একটি ভালো সিদ্ধান্ত অনেক বছর ধরে তোমাকে সাহায্য করবে। আমি নিশ্চিত, তোমার সততা ও কঠোর পরিশ্রম তোমাকে আরও উজ্জ্বল লক্ষ্যে পৌঁছাতে সাহায্য করবে। তোমার ভালো অভ্যাসগুলো ধরে রাখো, বিনয়ী থেকো এবং যেসব সহপাঠী এখনো উন্নতি করার চেষ্টা করছে তাদের সাহায্য করো। আমি প্রার্থনা করি, এইচএসসি পরীক্ষায় ও সামনের জীবনে তুমি আরও ভালো করবে। তোমার বাবা-মাকে আমার শ্রদ্ধা জানিও। Important Word Meanings English Word Bangla Meaning Delighted আনন্দিত Congratulations অভিনন্দন Achievement অর্জন Determination দৃঢ় সংকল্প Pride গর্ব Discipline শৃঙ্খলা Thoughtfully ভেবেচিন্তে Humble বিনয়ী Honesty সততা Brilliant উজ্জ্বল Exam Tips Learn the format first: address, date, salutation, body in three or four paragraphs, and a closing line with your name. plainContent: On this page you will find a letter about preparation for the examination, written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students. It gives the format of a personal letter, a full example letter describing how the writer is preparing for an examination, its Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. You can learn the letter for your examination and follow its study plan in your own preparation too. Format Your address at the top of the letter, on the right or left side as your teacher advises. The date below your address, so the reader knows when you wrote the letter. A greeting or salutation, such as "Dear Shila," to the friend you are writing to. The body of the letter, in three or four short paragraphs, describing your timetable, your revision, and your daily habits. A closing line, such as "Yours affectionately," followed by your name at the end of the letter. Simple and correct English throughout, with short sentences that are easy to understand. Letter: How I Am Preparing for the Examination (Example) Dear Shila, You asked about my examination preparation, so I am writing to tell you how I am getting ready. I made a timetable that divides each day into short study sessions and includes time for sleep, meals and exercise. I study the difficult subjects when my mind is fresh in the morning, and I keep the easier lessons for the afternoon. I follow the timetable every day, because a good plan is useful only when it is followed regularly. I am reviewing the difficult chapters first, and I am practising questions under time limits so that I can finish the paper in the examination hall. I keep a notebook of my mistakes, and I look at it before every test, because the same mistake should not happen twice. I also discuss confusing topics with my teachers instead of memorising blindly, and they explain the ideas in a simple way that I can remember. Each week I revise earlier lessons so that they do not fade from my memory. I read my notes again, solve a few old questions, and mark the parts I still find hard. I am trying to remain calm and avoid wasting time on my phone, because too much time on the phone breaks my concentration. I sleep on time and eat well, since a tired mind cannot learn properly. A farmer may work under strong sun or heavy rain and wait months before knowing whether the harvest will succeed. Floods, drought, cyclones, disease, and insects can destroy crops. Farmers need fair prices, quality seed, affordable credit, irrigation, and storage. Their contribution is fundamental to national life, so agriculture deserves sustained public support. Better roads and markets can reduce waste between field and consumer, and crop insurance can protect farmers from a bad season. My Village Paragraph in 300 Words Best for SSC and HSC. My village is a quiet community where people live close to fields, ponds, trees, and one another. It is not a large place, yet its green landscape and friendly people make it special to me. Farmers form the largest group, while teachers, shopkeepers, office workers, fishers, and other professionals also contribute to village life. People of different religions live together respectfully and share one another's joys and difficulties. In my village, a neighbour's problem is everyone's problem, and a wedding or a festival is celebrated by the whole village. The village has primary and secondary schools, a market, a health centre, a post office, and places of worship. A paved road joins it to the main highway, and smaller roads connect the neighbourhoods. The fields become bright with crops during the growing season, and a canal, shady trees, gardens, and open sky add to the scenery. Fresh vegetables, fish, milk, and clean air are among the benefits of rural life. In the morning, birds sing and farmers go to the fields, and in the evening, children play in the open ground. Although modern facilities are increasing, the village still retains its calm character. Electricity, mobile phones, and better roads have reached us, but people still help one another in times of need, and neighbours know each other by name. I love my village because it is beautiful, cooperative, and closely connected to nature. I hope to help its people prosper while preserving its peaceful environment, so that the next generation can also grow up in this calm and green place. Many people who move to the city for work still dream of their village, and they return home for festivals and holidays. The village lives in their hearts wherever they go. I am proud of my village. I divide large chapters into small tasks. Sajib: I often lose an hour to my phone and then try to study late at night. Nayeem: A schedule helps. Keep the phone away during study periods and set a clear stopping time. Short breaks make the work easier. Sajib: Do you study all day? Nayeem: No. I leave time for sleep, meals, exercise, prayer, and family. Using time well means giving each duty its proper place, not remaining busy every minute. plainContent: A lively meeting place for readers A book fair is a temporary marketplace where publishers, booksellers, writers, and readers meet. Rows of colourful stalls display storybooks, novels, science books, biographies, dictionaries, and works by local authors. Visitors can examine new publications, compare prices, and often meet writers at discussions or signing sessions. The event is enjoyable, but its greatest value is educational. It introduces children to many kinds of reading and encourages families to make books part of everyday life. Publishers also use the fair to present new ideas and support young writers. A fair may include lectures, quizzes, exhibitions, and cultural programmes as well. When I visit one, I make a list before entering so that excitement does not make me waste money. title: The Ant and the Grasshopper Completing Story
excerpt: Throughout the warm months, an ant carried grains to a dry store beneath a tree. Nearby, a grasshopper spent the days singing and resting in the sun. The ant
plainContent: The Ant and the Grasshopper Throughout the warm months, an ant carried grains to a dry store beneath a tree. Nearby, a grasshopper spent the days singing and resting in the sun. The ant invited him to gather food before winter, but the grasshopper replied that there was plenty of time. The ant continued working a little every day. He did not refuse rest or happiness; he simply prepared before the weather changed. Soon cold rain covered the fields, insects disappeared, and the grasshopper found nothing to eat. Hungry and shivering, he went to the ant’s shelter and asked for help. The ant shared a small meal but explained that kindness could not replace planning. He advised the grasshopper to gather food whenever spring returned and to balance enjoyment with responsibility. The grasshopper understood that he had confused leisure with a life without duties. When warm weather came again, he worked beside the ant each morning and sang only after storing enough food. The two friends remained helpful to one another. Moral: Prepare during good times, and do not sacrifice necessary work for immediate pleasure.

Families use it for communication, shopping, banking, entertainment, and work. Users must remember that not everything online is true or safe. We should compare reliable sources, use strong passwords, keep accounts private, and never harass another person. Spending too much time online can also damage sleep and study habits. title: Our National Flag Paragraph for Class 6, 7, 8, SSC and HSC
excerpt: A national flag gives a country a visible sign of identity and independence. Bangladesh’s flag is a green rectangle carrying a red circle slightly toward the
plainContent: Our National Flag A national flag gives a country a visible sign of identity and independence. Bangladesh’s flag is a green rectangle carrying a red circle slightly toward the hoist. The green recalls the country’s fertile land and lively natural landscape. The red suggests the rising sun as well as the sacrifice made during the struggle for freedom. The flag was designed by artist Kamrul Hassan in its present form. An earlier wartime design included a map of Bangladesh, but the map was later removed so that the flag would remain clear and easy to reproduce. The first version was raised publicly at the University of Dhaka on 2 March 1971, before independence was achieved. The proportions of the flag are 10 units in length to 6 units in width. It is flown on Independence Day, Victory Day, national ceremonies, schools, government buildings, and international occasions. Students should handle it carefully, keep it clean, and never allow it to touch the ground. Respect for the flag is respect for the people and history it represents.

An educated woman can care for her health, earn a living, understand her rights, and contribute to family and national development. Keeping girls in school also benefits future generations. Mothers who have received education are more likely to value vaccination, nutrition, and schooling for their children. Yet poverty, unsafe travel, early marriage, and social prejudice still prevent many girls from continuing their studies. Families, schools, and government should work together to remove these obstacles. Supporting female education creates opportunity, reduces inequality, and strengthens society.

plainContent: Keeping the environment clean Air, water, and soil become polluted when smoke, chemicals, sewage, plastic, and other waste are released carelessly. Polluted surroundings can cause illness, kill fish and plants, reduce soil fertility, and make cities uncomfortable to live in. Factories and vehicles should use cleaner methods, and authorities must collect waste and treat sewage properly. Citizens also have responsibilities: they should use bins, reduce plastic, save water and electricity, plant trees, and avoid burning rubbish. Environmental protection is not an occasional campaign. It is a daily practice shared by households, schools, businesses, and government. Clean surroundings support healthy lives and a safer future.

plainContent: Mobile Phone A mobile phone is a portable device used for calls, messages, photography, internet access, navigation, learning, and emergency assistance. Students can use educational applications, dictionaries, recorded lessons, and online libraries. Families can remain connected even when members live in different places. The device becomes harmful when it controls the user. Excessive gaming and social media can reduce sleep, attention, physical activity, and face-to-face conversation. Distracted driving, unsafe sharing of photographs, scams, and cyberbullying are additional risks. We should keep phones away during study and meals, protect personal information, and follow school and road rules. A phone is useful equipment when guided by self-control.

title: Road Accident Paragraph
excerpt: A road accident is a collision or other harmful incident involving vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, or roadside objects. It may occur on a highway, street,
plainContent: Road Accidents A road accident is a collision or other harmful incident involving vehicles, pedestrians, cyclists, or roadside objects. It may occur on a highway, street, bridge, or village road. Speeding, reckless overtaking, driving while tired, using a phone, ignoring signals, and driving an unfit vehicle are common causes. Poor lighting, damaged roads, untrained drivers, and careless pedestrians add to the danger. Accidents cause death, injury, disability, emotional pain, and financial loss. A single crash can affect an entire family and delay traffic for thousands of people. Safety begins with behaviour: drivers should obey speed limits, wear seat belts or helmets, avoid alcohol and phones, and never drive when exhausted. Pedestrians should use footpaths and crossings where available and look carefully before crossing. Authorities must enforce licensing rules, inspect vehicles, repair roads, improve signs and lighting, and educate the public. Emergency services should be able to reach crash sites quickly. Road safety is a shared responsibility. Patience and respect for traffic rules can save lives that no later punishment can restore.

title: Dialogue How to Make a Good Result
excerpt: Kamal: Examinations are approaching, and I do not know how to organize my preparation.
plainContent: Building strong study habits Kamal: Examinations are approaching, and I do not know how to organize my preparation. Jamal: Begin with a realistic timetable. List every subject, identify weak chapters, and assign short study periods with breaks. Kamal: I usually read the textbook repeatedly but forget it during the test. Jamal: Close the book and recall the main points. Solve practice questions, explain a lesson aloud, and review mistakes rather than merely rereading. Kamal: Should I study all night? Jamal: No. Adequate sleep, nutritious food, exercise, and a calm mind improve memory. Keep your phone away during focused study and ask teachers about difficult topics. Kamal: I also lose marks because I rush. Jamal: Practise writing within a time limit. In the examination, read directions carefully, plan long answers, and leave a few minutes for checking. Kamal: I will start today and measure progress by completed tasks, not by hours spent at the desk. Jamal: That is a sensible approach. Consistent effort usually produces better results than last-minute pressure.

title: Advantage & Disadvantage of Village life and City life Dialogue

plainContent: Comparing rural and urban living Rasel: Would you prefer to live in a village or a city? Mita: I enjoy village life because it is quieter, greener, and closer to fields and open water. Neighbours often know one another and help during difficulties. Rasel: Cities offer more colleges, hospitals, jobs, libraries, and cultural events. Public transport and internet services may also be easier to find. Mita: That is true, but cities can be crowded, noisy, polluted, and expensive. Villages may have limited specialist healthcare, employment, and reliable transport. Rasel: Rural areas are changing too. Better roads, schools, and digital connections can provide opportunities without destroying their peaceful character. Mita: And cities can learn from villages by protecting open spaces, reducing pollution, and encouraging community relationships. Rasel: Neither way of life is perfect. The right choice depends on a person’s work, family, and needs. Mita: Improving both places is more useful than arguing that one is always superior.

title: Discipline Composition
excerpt: On this page you will find a discipline composition with an outline, the full composition, a Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. It is
plainContent: On this page you will find a discipline composition with an outline, the full composition, a Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. It is written in simple English for Class 6 to 10, SSC and HSC students, so you can learn the main points easily and write the composition in your own words in the examination hall. Outline What discipline is: following rules and doing duties on time Discipline in the daily life of a student Discipline at home, at school, at work and in public life Life without discipline: talent wasted How to build discipline step by step: small habits and a realistic daily routine Conclusion: discipline is the key to success Discipline Composition Discipline means following good rules and doing our duties at the proper time. It does not mean fear or punishment; it means controlling ourselves so that a small comfort today does not destroy a big goal tomorrow. A disciplined person wakes up on time, keeps his things in order, finishes his work on time, and respects the rules of his family, school and society. Discipline is not a burden. It is a habit that makes life orderly, peaceful and successful. Just as a train cannot run without rails, a person cannot reach his goal without discipline. Discipline is most important in the life of a student. A disciplined student attends classes regularly, listens to his teachers, studies every day, and submits his homework on time. He keeps his books and notes tidy, prepares his lessons before class, and never copies in the examination. He respects his teachers and classmates, speaks politely, and follows the rules of his school. Such a student earns the love of his teachers and the trust of his friends, and he moves steadily towards success. Discipline is also needed outside school. At home, it means helping parents, keeping things in their place, and eating and sleeping on time. At work, it means arriving on time and finishing duties with care. In public life, it means obeying traffic rules, standing in a queue, keeping the roads and parks clean, and keeping promises. Discipline also teaches us to respect the rights of others. When people follow such rules, society becomes peaceful and safe. A country cannot progress if its people do not follow discipline. Without discipline, even talent is wasted. A clever student may fail because he studies only at the last moment. A strong player may lose because he does not practise regularly. Discipline turns small daily efforts into great skill, and it builds self-respect, because a person learns that he can depend on his own decisions. But discipline should be realistic: we must keep time for sleep, play, family and rest, or it will become a burden. With patience and daily practice, discipline becomes a habit, and that habit is the key to success in life. Let us practise discipline every day, from small things, and build a better future. It is the time to learn, to build character, and to prepare for the future. A student does not study only to pass examinations; he studies to gain knowledge, to form good habits, and to become a useful citizen. The lessons and habits we learn in student life stay with us for our whole life. That is why student life is often called the seed time of life, because the seeds we sow now will grow into the fruits of our future. The first duty of a student is sincere study. He should attend classes regularly, listen to his teachers carefully, and ask questions when he does not understand a lesson. He should study every day, finish his homework on time, and revise his lessons before they are forgotten. A good student keeps his books and notes tidy, reads books outside his textbooks, and tries to understand his lessons instead of memorising them without meaning. He should also learn from his mistakes and never copy in an examination. Regular study, not study at the last moment, brings real success. Student life is not only about books. A student should also build a good character. He should respect his parents and teachers, love his classmates, speak the truth, and keep his promises. He should be disciplined and punctual, and he should take part in games, sports and cultural activities. Games keep the body healthy and the mind fresh, and they teach teamwork and fair play. A student may also join social work, which teaches kindness and responsibility towards others. Student life also has problems. Many students feel pressure about examinations, and some waste their time on the phone or in bad company. A student should face these problems with courage. He should keep a daily routine, sleep well, eat healthy food, and ask his teachers or parents for help when he faces a difficulty. If a student uses his time well, studies with sincerity, and keeps a good character, he can build a bright future for himself and for his country. In short, student life is the golden time of life, and we should use it wisely. Outline What time is and why it cannot be bought back How wise people use time: planning, a daily routine and clear priorities How time is wasted: laziness, delay and useless habits The results of using time well and wasting it Why students must learn the value of time early Conclusion: time is life, so use every moment well Value of Time Composition Time is the most valuable thing in our life. We can earn money again if we lose it, and we can recover our health with care and treatment, but a moment that has passed can never come back. Time moves forward all the time, and it waits for nobody. That is why wise people say that time is more precious than gold. Every person gets the same twenty-four hours in a day, but some use those hours well and rise in life, while others waste them and fall behind. A wise person uses time with a plan. He fixes his daily work, gives study, rest, play and family their proper time, and begins his work on time. A student should make a daily routine, study every subject a little every day, and finish his homework before the last moment. When a big task comes, he should divide it into small parts and finish one part each day. In this way, no work becomes too heavy, and the mind stays free from worry. Punctuality is also a part of using time well, because a punctual person earns the trust of others. On the other hand, many people waste time without knowing it. They sit idle, keep putting off their work for tomorrow, and spend hours on useless chatting and scrolling on the phone. This habit is called procrastination, and it is the greatest enemy of success. When work is left for the last moment, it becomes a burden, and the result is poor. A student who wastes his time in class and at home cannot do well in the examination, however clever he may be. Lost time brings regret, but regret cannot bring back the lost hours. So we should value time from today. We should set small goals, keep a routine, and do our daily work in time. We should also keep time for rest and play, because a tired mind cannot work well. A person who uses his time well can learn more, do more, and live a happier life. Let us remember that time is life itself. If we waste time, we waste our life. If we use time well, we can build a bright future for ourselves and for our country. plainContent: Dengue fever and prevention Dengue is a viral illness spread mainly by infected Aedes mosquitoes. These mosquitoes often breed in small amounts of water collected in buckets, flowerpots, tyres, roof gutters, or uncovered tanks. A patient may develop sudden fever, headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain, nausea, or a rash. Anyone with these symptoms should contact a qualified health professional, especially if the fever is high or persistent. Bleeding, repeated vomiting, abdominal pain, unusual sleepiness, or difficulty breathing are warning signs that require urgent care. Self-medication can be risky, so advice from a doctor is important. Families can reduce risk by emptying containers, cleaning drains, covering stored water, wearing protective clothing, and using approved mosquito protection. Schools and local authorities should keep public areas clean and spread accurate information. Community action is the strongest defence against dengue.

Outline What a newspaper is: printed and digital What we find inside a newspaper every day How a newspaper helps students How a newspaper helps society How to read a newspaper wisely and carefully Conclusion: a daily habit for an informed life Newspaper Composition A newspaper is a publication that comes out every day and tells us what is happening in our country and in the world. It may be printed on paper, or we may read it on a website or in an app on a mobile phone. Many newspapers are now published in both Bangla and English. A newspaper has many parts: national news, international news, education, science, health, business, sports, culture, weather, and advertisements. It also has editorials, letters from readers, and articles that explain important matters. In short, a newspaper is a storehouse of daily knowledge. A newspaper is very useful for students. A student who reads a newspaper every day learns many new words and improves his English. He learns about his country, the world, science, and sports, and he gets new ideas for essays, paragraphs and discussions. Reading the newspaper also helps him in examinations, because many questions in general knowledge and current affairs come from daily news. A student should read the newspaper for at least twenty minutes every day and note down new words and important facts in a notebook. A newspaper also helps society. It informs people about the decisions of the government, so they can understand their rights and duties. It exposes wrongdoing and corruption, and it speaks for people whose voices are not heard. It spreads new ideas about health, education, farming and technology, and it encourages people to think about problems and find solutions. It also publishes job advertisements, examination notices and useful information for students and job seekers. In this way, a newspaper builds public opinion and helps a country move forward on the right path. But a newspaper must be read with care. Not everything printed is true, and some news may be one-sided or incomplete. A wise reader checks the source, looks at the date, and compares the same news in more than one paper before believing it. News and opinion should not be confused: an editorial is the opinion of the paper, not a fact. We should also avoid spending all our time on sensational news. If we read a good newspaper every day with an open and careful mind, it will make us informed, thoughtful and responsible citizens. plainContent: On this page you will find an aim in life composition with an outline, the full composition, a Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips. Outline What an aim in life is and why everyone needs one My aim: to become a teacher Why I have chosen this aim How I will prepare myself for it What I will do after reaching my aim Conclusion: an aim gives life a direction Aim in Life Composition An aim in life is a clear idea about what a person wants to become and what kind of work he wants to do. Every person should have an aim, because without an aim, life is like a boat without a rudder: it drifts in any direction and reaches nowhere. A person with an aim knows what to study, how to use his time, and how to face difficulties. An aim gives life a direction, and it gives a person the courage to work hard every day. My aim in life is to become a teacher. I have chosen this aim because education changes lives. A good teacher can open the minds of students, explain difficult lessons in simple words, and encourage shy learners to speak and ask questions. In our villages, many children still do not get good teaching, and I want to work for them. A teacher does not earn as much money as a doctor or an engineer, but the respect and love a teacher receives from students is a great reward. I want to become a teacher who makes learning easy and joyful for every child. To reach my aim, I must prepare myself from now. I must study regularly, read books outside my textbooks, and improve my English and Bangla. I must learn to speak clearly, to explain ideas in simple words, and to listen patiently to others. I must also build a good character, because a teacher must be honest, kind and disciplined. I will take advice from my teachers, learn from their methods, and practise teaching my younger brothers and sisters at home. Step by step, I will make myself ready for this noble profession. After becoming a teacher, I will serve my students with sincerity. I will try to make my lessons interesting, help weak students with extra care, and never behave rudely with anyone. I will also encourage my students to love their country, to respect their parents, and to help others. An aim is not only for personal success; it is also for serving society. If I can become a good teacher, I will feel that my life has a true meaning. That is why I will work hard every day to reach my aim in life. title: The Pied Piper of Hamelin Completing Story
excerpt: The town of Hamelin was overrun by rats. They entered houses, spoiled food, and frightened the people. The mayor promised a large reward to anyone who could
plainContent: The Pied Piper of Hamelin The town of Hamelin was overrun by rats. They entered houses, spoiled food, and frightened the people. The mayor promised a large reward to anyone who could rid the town of the pests. A travelling piper arrived and said that his music could lead the rats away. He played a strange, bright tune, and every rat followed him through the streets and out to the river. He guided them safely away, then returned to claim the promised payment. The mayor had expected the piper to work for less and refused to pay the full reward. The piper warned him that a promise made publicly must be honoured, but the mayor dismissed him. The piper then played another tune. This time the town’s children followed him beyond the gates. When the mayor and citizens realised what was happening, they begged him to return them. The piper brought the children back only after the town paid what it had promised and apologised. From then on, Hamelin’s leaders kept their word. Moral: A promise is a responsibility, not an opportunity for dishonest bargaining.

title: Application for Transfer Certificate
excerpt: On this page you will find an application for a transfer certificate for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC students. It explains when you need this certificate, shows
plainContent: On this page you will find an application for a transfer certificate for Class 6 to 12, SSC and HSC students. It explains when you need this certificate, shows the correct format, and gives a complete example that you can follow in your examination. A Bangla meaning, important word meanings and exam tips are given at the end. Format of an Application for a Transfer Certificate A transfer certificate application follows the usual format of a formal application to the headmaster or principal. Each part has a fixed place, so learn the order first and then practise writing the full application. The main parts are given below. Date Name and designation of the headmaster or principal Name and address of the school Subject of the application Salutation, such as "Sir" Body of the application Closing, such as "Yours obediently" Name, class and roll number of the student A transfer certificate is an official paper from your old school. It proves that you were a student there and that you have cleared your dues. A new school asks for it before it admits you, so write the application in clear and polite language and mention your class and roll number correctly. Application for a Transfer Certificate (Example) 10 June 2026 The Headmaster Rangpur Zilla School Rangpur Subject: Request for a transfer certificate Sir, I respectfully state that I am a student of Class Ten in your school. My family will move to another district because my father has been transferred there, and I must continue my studies in a new school. The new school has asked me to submit a transfer certificate before it completes my admission. I have paid all my school dues and returned the books I borrowed from the library. I have also tried to follow the rules of the school and attend my classes regularly. My teachers know me well, and I have always tried to behave politely with my classmates. My father has already joined his new workplace, and our family will shift within a few weeks. For this reason I cannot continue my classes here for long. A transfer certificate will help me join the new school in time and continue my studies without a gap. I therefore request you to issue me a transfer certificate at your earliest convenience. I shall remain grateful to you for your kind help in this matter. I hope the new school will admit me without delay once I submit the certificate. Yours obediently, Rahim Class: Ten Roll: 12 Bangla Meaning of the Application for a Transfer Certificate ট্রান্সফার সার্টিফিকেটের আবেদনের বাংলা অর্থ আমি বিনীতভাবে জানাচ্ছি যে আমি আপনার স্কুলের দশম শ্রেণির একজন ছাত্র। আমার বাবার বদলির কারণে আমাদের পরিবার অন্য জেলায় চলে যাবে, তাই আমাকে সেখানেই পড়াশোনা চালিয়ে যেতে হবে। নতুন স্কুল ভর্তির আগে আমার কাছ থেকে ট্রান্সফার সার্টিফিকেট চেয়েছে। আমি স্কুলের সব বেতন পরিশোধ করেছি এবং লাইব্রেরি থেকে নেওয়া বইগুলো ফেরত দিয়েছি। আমি স্কুলের নিয়ম মেনে চলার চেষ্টা করেছি এবং নিয়মিত ক্লাসে উপস্থিত থেকেছি। আমার বাবা ইতিমধ্যে নতুন কর্মস্থলে যোগ দিয়েছেন এবং কয়েক সপ্তাহের মধ্যে আমাদের পরিবার সেখানে চলে যাবে। তাই আমি আর বেশিদিন এখানে ক্লাস করতে পারব না। ট্রান্সফার সার্টিফিকেট পেলে আমি সময়মতো নতুন স্কুলে ভর্তি হতে পারব এবং পড়াশোনায় কোনো ফাঁক পড়বে না। তাই আমি অনুরোধ করছি, আপনি যেন যত তাড়াতাড়ি সম্ভব আমাকে একটি ট্রান্সফার সার্টিফিকেট দেন। সার্টিফিকেটটি জমা দিলে নতুন স্কুল আমাকে দেরি না করে ভর্তি করবে বলে আমি আশা করি। আপনার এই সাহায্যের জন্য আমি কৃতজ্ঞ থাকব। একটি ট্রান্সফার সার্টিফিকেট পুরনো স্কুলের একটি সরকারি কাগজ। এটি প্রমাণ করে যে তুমি সেখানে পড়তে এবং তোমার সব বকেয়া পরিশোধ করা হয়েছে। নতুন স্কুল ভর্তির আগে এটি চায়, তাই আবেদনে নিজের শ্রেণি ও রোল নম্বর সঠিকভাবে লিখতে হবে এবং ভাষা হতে হবে ভদ্র ও পরিষ্কার। Important Word Meanings Learn these words before you write the application. They will help you understand the example and write similar applications in your own words. Keep the format in the correct order: date, headmaster, school address, subject, salutation, body, closing, and then your name, class and roll number. Write the body in three short paragraphs: introduce yourself and give the reason, show that your dues are clear, and then make your request politely. Do not memorise the example word by word. Check your spelling, the subject line and your class and roll number before you finish, because a small mistake can cost marks.
